scenarioResults.finding: Reviewer reported PASS during the real Orca session and stated that the page structure and interactive elements were read aloud accurately while navigating and activating controls with the keyboard.
Reviewer reported PASS after checking accessible names, roles, states, and values with Orca, describing the announcements as accurate and prompt.
Reviewer reported PASS after exercising keyboard focus navigation with Orca and described the focus announcements as accurate.
Reviewer reported PASS after triggering the background live-region status update with Orca and described the dynamic announcement as accurate.
Reviewer reported PASS after selecting the Permission required state and reviewing its Orca presentation, describing the announced result as accurate.
Reviewer reported PASS after selecting the Restricted state and reviewing its Orca presentation, describing the announced result as accurate.
Reviewer reported PASS after selecting the Offline state and reviewing its Orca presentation, describing the announced result as accurate.
Reviewer reported PASS after selecting the Error state and reviewing its Orca presentation and recovery wording, describing the announced result as accurate.
Reviewer reported PASS after reviewing the loading/progress control through Orca and described the progress announcement as accurate.
Reviewer reported PASS after increasing Firefox zoom and navigating the enlarged interface with Orca, describing the continued assistive-technology presentation as accurate.

laneEvidence.finding: A real Orca 42.0 session in Firefox 156.0 on Zorin OS 17.3 passed all ten governed assistive-technology scenarios using keyboard navigation, including semantic structure, control semantics, focus, dynamic announcements, state distinctions, progress, and zoom continuity.

The same real Orca session independently supports the Accessibility assistive-technology alternative through successful semantic navigation, accessible name/role/state review, focus announcements, live-region behavior, state communication, progress exposure, and large-text/zoom continuity.
